title: Myles Garrett's girlfriend won Olympic gold twice, but she was privately struggling the entire time - NewsBreak
text:
By Brendan McGilligan ,
6 hours ago Photo by Jun Sato and WireImage Los Angeles Rams star Myles Garrett is a major name in the NFL and will be proud of the success he has achieved in his football career. However, he will never be able to claim the silverware his girlfriend has won in her career. Chloe Kim is a two-time Olympic gold medallist and is one of the greatest women’s snowboarders in the world. Obviously, football is not an Olympic sport, so unless Garrett switches sports, he will never emulate her success.
Kim has been incredibly successful in her snowboarding career. Along with her two Olympic gold medals in the women’s halfpipe, she has three gold medals at the FIS Snowboarding World Championships in the same event. She also won eight X Games gold medals in the SuperPipe event. However, over this period, it has now been revealed that Kim has been dealing with some struggles, and she has finally opened up about them.
The 26-year-old has revealed that she has finally been diagnosed with ADHD (Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder). Kim spoke about her struggles in a promotional video she shared on Instagram . After she spoke to her doctor about her struggles, they were able to diagnose her. The Olympian revealed that once she was diagnosed, everything made sense. Kim is just one of several high-performing athletes who have ADHD.
High-profile athletes with ADHD ADHD is a common neurodevelopmental condition marked by ongoing patterns of inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity. Several high-profile athletes have been diagnosed with this condition. Kim is just the latest to speak publicly about having ADHD. This should be viewed as a positive, as it may encourage young individuals to embrace being diagnosed with the condition and be inspired by these athletes achieving incredible success despite having ADHD.
It has been reported by ADDitude that up to 8% of athletes have the condition, compared to 2% to 7% of the general population. This publication goes on to list 22 athletes who have been diagnosed with ADHD. It includes Olympic gymnast Simone Biles, former NBA star Kevin Garnett, and the most decorated Olympian of all time, Michael Phelps.
Other major athletes who have been diagnosed with ADHD include British boxer Nicola Adams and five-time Olympic medalist Justin Gatlin. Meanwhile, Tom Holland, who plays Spider-Man, and Harry Potter star Emma Watson have also been diagnosed with ADHD.
